author: l. t. aponte
title: Harriet Hageman shares legislative priorities and constituent meetings on April 15
text:
Rep. Harriet Hageman, who represents Wyoming’s at-large district in the U.S. Congress, posted a series of updates on April 15, 2026, highlighting meetings with constituents and legislative initiatives related to transportation safety and federal accountability.
On April 15, Hageman shared a message about her participation in constituent meetings in Washington D.C., stating: “Wyoming Wednesday is in session! Great meeting with constituents in D.C. alongside @SenJohnBarrasso and @SenLummis.”
Later that day, she expressed gratitude for support from the American Trucking Associations regarding her SAFE Act bill: ‘”You can’t enforce safety at scale without the people and systems to do it.” Thank you @TRUCKINGdotORG for supporting my bill, the SAFE Act, to deliver more resources for @SecDuffy and @USDOT to crack down on chameleon carriers everywhere.’
In another post from April 15, Hageman addressed concerns about the enforcement of the FACE Act by the Department of Justice under President Biden’s administration: “The Biden DOJ weaponized the FACE Act against pro-life Americans, and those responsible must be held accountable. I introduced the First Amendment Accountability Act to hold federal employees individually liable for violating your constitutional rights.”
Harriet Hageman has served as Wyoming’s sole member of the U.S. House since replacing Liz Cheney in 2023. Born in Fort Laramie in 1962 and currently residing in Cheyenne, Hageman earned both her BS and JD degrees from the University of Wyoming in 1989.
